name: 6-Bid Solo
description: 6-Bid Solo: 3p trick-taking from German Tarok/Skat; popular in Salt Lake City. 36 cards; 11 each, 3-card widow. Bids: Solo (60+ pts), Heart Solo, Misère, Guarantee (74/80), Spread Misère, Call Solo (120). A-10-K-Q-J-9-8-7-6; 120 pts per round.

content.text: 6-Bid Solo: 3p trick-taking from German Tarok/Skat; popular in Salt Lake City. 36 cards; 11 each, 3-card widow. Bids: Solo (60+ pts), Heart Solo, Misère, Guarantee (74/80), Spread Misère, Call Solo (120). A-10-K-Q-J-9-8-7-6; 120 pts per round.

Six-Bid Solo is an American three-player point-trick game in the German Ace-Ten tradition. It descends from the 36-card game Tappen (German Tarok), which was played in southern Germany, western Austria and Switzerland in the early 19th century and later gave rise to local American variants.
36 cards: A, 10, K, Q, J, 9, 8, 7, 6 in four suits (French). One standard 52-card deck with 2s, 3s, 4s, 5s removed.
36-card deck, score sheet or chips for point settlement.

Deal a batch of 4 cards to each player, then 3 to each, then 3 cards face down in the center (widow), then 4 more to each. Eleven cards per player; the widow stays unseen until the end. Deal clockwise starting from the player to the dealer's left.
